item.title: Florida Senate race set between Ashley Moody and Angie Nixon
item.description: GOP Sen. Ashley Moody and Democratic State Rep. Angie Nixon will face off in November after winning their primaries for U.S. Senate on Tuesday night, the Associated Press projects.

item.title: Justice Department to send record 1,000 monitors to polling places for midterm elections
item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division announced Monday that she's planning to deploy 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections. Jen Fifield, reporter for ProPublica, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Meta's federal trial begins over child social media addiction claims
item.description: The lawsuit accuses the social media giant of contributing to the youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing features that addict children to its platforms.

item.title: Details on Meta trial over child social media addiction claims
item.description: Meta is standing trial over claims that it intentionally designed its products to be addictive and therefore harmful to children. Lance Ulanoff, editor-at-large at TechRadar, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's former mother-in-law says she was "begging for help" as murder trial continues
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's former mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, took the stand Tuesday to offer testimony as Lindsay Clancy stands on trial for the killings of her three children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Southern U.S. under extreme weather advisory as "heat dome," humidity build
item.description: 70 million people in southern U.S. states from Texas to the Carolinas are scorching in the sun amid a major heat wave. Rob Marciano has the story and the forecast.

item.title: Trump says no talks with Iran planned as he posts map labeling Strait of Hormuz as U.S. territory
item.description: President Trump posted an image showing the Strait of Hormuz labeled as a U.S. territory on Tuesday. Mr. Trumps says no new talks with Iran are planned. CBS News' Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Debbie Wasserman Schultz wins primary for Florida's new 20th district, AP projects
item.description: Debbie Wasserman Schultz has won the Democratic primary for Florida's newly configured 20th district, the Associated Press projects. CBS News' Nikole Killion and Anthony Salvanto have more.

item.title: Scandal-ridden Cory Mills ousted in GOP primary in Florida's 7th District
item.description: The Trump-backed incumbent has struggled to raise money for his reelection bid as the House Ethics Committee investigates numerous allegations against him.

item.title: Byron Donalds, David Jolly to face off in Florida governor's race
item.description: Rep. Byron Donalds won the Republican primary for governor and former Rep. David Jolly won the Democratic primary, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with drones as Russia threatens U.K. over support
item.description: Ukraine targets Moscow with a huge wave of drones as Russia warns the U.K. will pay a price for supplying Kyiv with long-range weapons.

item.title: Tupac Shakur autopsy photos shown at murder trial after some family members leave
item.description: Tupac Shakur's cousin said the autopsy photos made him feel "very angry, to say the least."

item.title: Panettiere was with on-and-off boyfriend when she died, police report says
item.description: Brian Hickerson and his brother, Zach, made the 911 call that brought first responders to the apartment where Hayden Panettiere was found unresponsive.

item.title: NASA images show 60-foot-wide crater on moon after SpaceX rocket booster crash
item.description: A NASA spacecraft circling the moon is providing the sharpest views yet of the crater carved by a crashing SpaceX rocket.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy said a voice ordered her to kill children, psychologist testifies
item.description: A psychologist who met with Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after her children's deaths testified Tuesday at her Massachusetts murder trial.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: Frank Beard, ZZ Top drummer, dies at age 77
item.description: "Today, Elwood and I lost a great friend and collaborator, and the world lost one of the most naturally innovative drummers and a great and true son of Texas," ZZ Top's Billy Gibbons said in a statement.

item.title: Who is Natalie Harp? Trump's loyal assistant suddenly in the spotlight
item.description: The 35-year-old executive assistant to the president is a quiet but loyal force at President Trump's side.

item.title: State Farm is sending refund checks to customers. Here's who qualifies.
item.description: More than 7.2 million checks have been mailed so far, with millions more expected to go out this week, according to State Farm.

item.title: U.S. deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala and Honduras, angering Mexico
item.description: The Trump administration has been quietly deporting migrants from Mexico to Central America, despite the Mexican government's willingness to accept the return of all its citizens.

item.title: Newsom may veto bill giving California high-speed rail watchdog more power, sources say
item.description: Critics called it the "anti-transparency" bill. Newsom quietly enacted the controversial part and may now veto the part the rail watchdog says he needs, sources tell CBS California.

item.title: Human remains found in Lake Mead as water levels reach record low
item.description: The skeletal remains were found on Sunday, two years after similar drought conditions exposed bodies in the lake.

item.title: California high-speed rail could run out of money by December 2027, as authority cuts train order in half
item.description: The watchdog's review warns the $4 billion federal funding loss now leaves the project needing billions in financing within 16 months — as the rail authority acknowledges for the first time that it still has no train contract, has cut its order from six trains to three, and has dropped the "Buy America" requirement.

item.title: What's behind the $4B funding cut for California's high-speed rail?
item.description: Records reveal California twice missed deadlines to buy the trains at the center of a federal funding fight — then quietly dropped its lawsuit weeks after missing its new deadline.

item.title: California diaper program could "lead to waste," state records warned
item.description: Records reveal repeated warnings that Baby2Baby's plan to send every baby home with 400 diapers in limited sizes could lead to waste.

item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: Newsom's office called our diaper contract reporting "demonstrably false." State records show what happened
item.description: Gov. Newsom's office says the no-bid deal was "competitive," the records weren't delayed, and our reporting is false. The state's own database, deadlines, and the Legislature's budget bills say otherwise. Here's the point-by-point review.

item.title: Newsom's "competitive bid" diaper deal wasn't. California's budget includes dozens of similar no-bid exemptions.
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom said the $6.2 million Baby2Baby contract "went through a competitive bidding process." State records reveal it didn't. CBS California Investigates found dozens of similar no-bid deals in the state budget worth over $1 billion.

item.title: California still hasn't released Baby2Baby diaper contract as lawmakers weigh longer public records delays
item.description: The Newsom administration waited 24 days to decide if it would even let Californians see the multi-million-dollar contract with Baby2Baby, a nonprofit linked to First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom.

item.title: Critics got California's free diaper math wrong, but state won't release key Baby2Baby records
item.description: A CBS News California fact-check found the state's free diaper program won't cost taxpayers 50 cents per diaper, as viral posts claimed. But the Newsom administration still won't release the Baby2Baby contract or competitive bid records amid concerns free diapers could go to waste.
